cover.title: 6 metrics that will make you a disgustingly bad founder

inner.title: raw pageviews
inner.body: pageviews count every load, including the ones nobody read. across 2 billion visits, chartbeat found 55% spent under 15 seconds actively on the page.

inner.title: likes and shares
inner.body: likes and shares tell you a post traveled, not that anyone read it. chartbeat found no link between shares and attention across 10,000 articles.

inner.title: bounce rate
inner.body: in ga4, bounce rate is just the share of sessions that weren't engaged. stay 11 seconds, buy nothing, leave, and google counts you as engaged.

inner.title: signups without activation
inner.body: signups count people who opened the door, not people who walked in. the average android app loses 77% of daily users within three days.

inner.title: total registered users
inner.body: total registered users counts everyone who ever made an account, even the long gone. fred wilson's rule: about 30% use it monthly, 10% daily.

inner.title: waitlist size
inner.body: a waitlist counts emails typed once, with no money on the line. vc doug renert tells investors to check growth isn't just waitlists or launch press.

closer.HEADLINE:
stop counting visitors.
start counting habits.
closer.SUBLINE: one action that repeats beats a million views
closer.THIS_WEEK: chart weekly active users, not totals
closer.NEXT_WEEK: cut every metric nobody acts on
closer.NEXT_TITLE: 5 niche signs you're becoming a terrifyingly good founder
